assets.title: Breath, Sound, Body Meditation
assets.creator: UCLA Mindful (UCLA Health)
assets.summary: Seated practice using the breath as an anchor, with permission to shift attention to a strong sound or body sensation (including unpleasant ones) and then return to the breath; ends with kindness phrases.
learning_objectives: Use breath as an anchor
Notice sounds and body sensations with curiosity rather than story
Return to the breath when a sensation fades
practical_techniques: Anchor on breath at abdomen, chest or nostrils
Label wandering as "thinking" or "wandering" and redirect
Follow a dominant sound or sensation until it releases, then return to breath
Kindness phrases at the end
clinical_cautions: Guidance on unpleasant sensation is general ("Particularly if it's unpleasant"); no pain-specific caution is stated in the transcript

assets.title: Complete Meditation Instructions
assets.creator: UCLA Mindful (UCLA Health)
assets.summary: Longest UCLA item: full instruction in open-monitoring practice. Breath is home base; attention can move to sounds, body sensations, emotions (felt in the body and labelled), thoughts (labelled) and mood, always able to return to breath; silent periods and kindness phrases follow.
learning_objectives: Learn to move attention among breath, sound, sensation, emotion, thought and mood
Use the breath as a safe place to return to
practical_techniques: Let go of breath to follow a predominant sensation or sound, then return
Locate and label emotion in the body
Label repetitive thoughts (worrying, planning, remembering)
Check body sensations if a thought loop persists
clinical_cautions: Instructs attending to strong emotions and sensations; transcript advises "If it feels like too much always return to the breath"

assets.title: Loving Kindness Meditation
assets.creator: UCLA Mindful (UCLA Health)
assets.summary: Imagery-based practice: call to mind someone easy to love, offer wishes of safety, happiness, health and ease, receive them back, then direct them to self, a wider group and all beings.

Include oneself in kind wishes
practical_techniques: Visualise a loved one, pet or easy person
Silent repetition of well-wishing phrases (own words allowed)
Receive kindness back; extend to self and all beings
clinical_cautions: Transcript notes self-directed kindness is "not always easy" and that feeling nothing is fine; no clinical caution stated

assets.title: Meditation for Working with Difficulties
assets.creator: UCLA Mindful (UCLA Health)
assets.summary: Short practice for difficult emotions or body sensations (examples in the transcript include an aching shoulder or back and a headache): rest attention on a pleasant or neutral body area, briefly visit the difficulty, alternate between them, then keep about 75% of attention on the comfortable area while glancing at the difficulty, and close with kindness.
learning_objectives: Work with difficult sensation or emotion without being overwhelmed
Practise alternating attention between ease and difficulty
practical_techniques: Find a pleasant, safe or neutral body part (hands, feet, legs) and rest there
Briefly turn to the difficult sensation then return
75% of attention on the comfortable area, side-long glance at difficulty
Notice whether the sensation grows, shrinks or shifts
Kindness to self and shared suffering
clinical_cautions: Alternation is explicitly to give a break from what "could be potentially overwhelming to feel"; "Make sure to breathe"; no medical caution stated

assets.title: Body Scan for Sleep
assets.creator: UCLA Mindful (UCLA Health)
assets.summary: Lying-down body scan from head to toes (left side then right, then back, chest, pelvis, legs) framed for preparing for sleep; falling asleep is described as fine and the track may be left to end by itself.
learning_objectives: Wind down for sleep using body awareness
Meet tension and worries with gentle return to the scan
practical_techniques: Sequential scan with curiosity about vibration, tingling, heat, heaviness
Direct breath to a tense area to soften it, otherwise continue
Let worries pass "like clouds" and return to the scan
Repeat the scan, optionally feet to head
clinical_cautions: No pain-specific or medical caution stated; transcript says tension that does not release can simply be noticed

assets.summary: Five-part guided practice for physical pain (migraine, injury or surgery recovery, back pain, chronic pain): supported posture and breath; describing the pain's sensations (size, texture, shape, boundaries) and softening at its edges; naming the feeling about it; searching for pleasant or neutral body areas; broadening awareness so the pain is held inside something bigger (others share similar pain); then responding rather than reacting.
